## The Sacred Valley of the Incas: Pisac, Awanakancha and Ollantaytambo in one day

From [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), you can explore the [Sacred Valley of the Incas](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/) and encounter different aspects of Andean heritage in a single day. Our excursion includes 3 stops: the craft market at [Pisac](/peru/place/pisac/), [Awanakancha](/peru/place/awanakancha/), home to Andean camelids, and the [Ollantaytambo archaeological complex](/peru/place/ollantaytambo/).

**This is a full-day trip.** A buffet lunch at a restaurant specializing in national cuisine is included. The itinerary is particularly interesting because Inca history, modern craftsmanship and living highland traditions are experienced at actual sites rather than only from a vehicle.

## Pisac: the Sacred Valley's market and crafts

The program includes a visit to the craft market in [Pisac](/peru/place/pisac/), where you can see ceramics, wool products, silverwork and leather goods. The variety illustrates how local techniques and designs continue to feature in souvenirs and everyday objects.

The market appeals to travelers who like examining materials, learning the origins of patterns and selecting locally made products. It is important to distinguish handcrafted items from mass-produced souvenirs: their origins are not always obvious from appearance alone, so ask directly about the maker and materials.

Pisac is also known for archaeological landscapes and terraces. However, on this **specific** Ada Tours itinerary, the confirmed Pisac activity is primarily the craft market. A separate visit to the Pisac archaeological complex should not be assumed to be included without additional agreement.

## Awanakancha: llamas, alpacas and wool processing

At [Awanakancha](/peru/place/awanakancha/), the focus shifts to Andean animals and wool crafts. During our excursion, you encounter **llamas, alpacas, guanacos and vicunas** and learn about processing fibers and dyeing them with natural pigments.

This stop explains why woolen fabrics and products are so characteristic of the region. The animals differ in appearance and fiber properties, while fabric production involves several steps: obtaining fibers, preparing them, spinning, dyeing and weaving.

Awanakancha provides a different experience from simply buying a finished item at a market: travelers discover where materials come from and how local techniques work. Direct contact with or feeding animals, and participation in production, are not automatically permitted for every visitor. Follow the center staff's instructions.

## Ollantaytambo: stone terraces and an Inca town

[Ollantaytambo](/peru/place/ollantaytambo/) preserves monumental terraces, large stone structures and remains of Inca-era fortifications. This part of the excursion shows how ancient builders worked with mountainous terrain, used changes in elevation and positioned buildings on slopes.

While Awanakancha introduces living crafts, Ollantaytambo reveals the Incas' material culture. The scale of the masonry, stairways, walls and views of the valley are all part of the experience.

Comfortable footwear is essential at the archaeological site. Stone steps and altitude may make climbing difficult; those who prefer a gentler route should discuss the accessible parts of the visit in advance. Not everyone in the group needs to climb every section to appreciate the monument.

## What the 3 stops offer together

Each stop explores a different side of the region rather than repeating the same theme:

| Stop | Main focus |
|---|---|
| Pisac | Crafts and market |
| Awanakancha | Animals and wool |
| Ollantaytambo | Inca archaeology |

This sequence reveals connections between the Andean environment, local materials and the heritage of the valley's ancient inhabitants. On the road, you also see rivers, fields and slopes that shape the [Sacred Valley landscape](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/).

Travelers mainly seeking hiking or strenuous physical activities will find this a different kind of excursion. It centers on cultural sites, crafts and relatively short visits, although the full day of transfers is still busy.

## Practical considerations: altitude, roads and lunch

The excursion starts and ends in Cusco. During the day, you travel between several settlements and attractions with differing visiting conditions, so agree on departure time and pace in advance.

At high altitude, strong sunlight may coincide with cool air and rapidly changing weather. Closed-toe shoes, a hat, drinking water and layered clothing are useful. Consider how you feel after arriving in Cusco and avoid scheduling too many additional activities on the same day.

**A buffet lunch is included.** Confirm dishes and drinks beforehand, particularly if you have dietary restrictions.

On the [12-day Peru and Bolivia itinerary](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-uyuni-12-days/), this excursion is offered as a separate Sacred Valley option. A price of **$220** is listed for the excursion within that tour, but the pricing basis must be confirmed when selecting the trip.

## Frequently asked questions about the Sacred Valley excursion

### How long is needed for Pisac, Awanakancha and Ollantaytambo?

The complete excursion takes **a full day** from Cusco. Time at individual stops depends on travel and the agreed sequence.

### Is lunch included?

Yes. The excursion includes a buffet lunch at a restaurant serving national cuisine.

### Will we see llamas and alpacas?

Llamas, alpacas, guanacos and vicunas are listed at Awanakancha. The exact nature of interaction with animals follows the center's rules.

### Can we combine the Sacred Valley with Machu Picchu?

These areas work well on a longer Peru trip, but [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) is not automatically included in this excursion day. It requires separate time, transport and tickets.

## Cusco: stone structures, the Temple of the Sun and waterworks

This excursion introduces several aspects of Inca architecture. [Sacsayhuaman](/peru/place/sacsayhuaman/) features massive stone structures above the city; [Coricancha](/peru/place/coricancha/) was Cusco's religious center; and [Tambomachay](/peru/place/tambomachay/) illustrates the construction of channels and pools. The route links city landmarks with archaeological sites in the nearby hills.

## Sacsayhuaman and Coricancha

Sacsayhuaman is the first stop. You will see its massive walls and masonry, which form some of the archaeological site's most recognizable views. During the visit, compare the scale of individual stone blocks and how the structures sit within the surrounding landscape.

The excursion then continues to Coricancha, the Temple of the Sun. Surviving Inca walls and colonial buildings reveal different periods of history at one site. This is particularly illuminating for exploring [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), where ancient structures remain part of the modern urban setting.

## Tambomachay and the view of Puka Pukara

At Tambomachay, attention turns to Inca hydraulic engineering: stone channels, fountains and pools. Nearby is the [Puka Pukara complex](/peru/place/puka-pukara/), whose name is usually translated as "Red Fortress."

On this itinerary, Puka Pukara is viewed from outside near Tambomachay. We can agree separately on entry to the interior areas if it is important for your trip.

## How this excursion fits into our tour

On the [15-day journey through Brazil, Argentina, Chile and Peru](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-peru-15-days/), this excursion takes place on day fourteen. The previous day, you visit Machu Picchu and return to Cusco for the night. After exploring the archaeological sites, you transfer to the airport, fly to Lima and check into a hotel.

The excursion and its scheduled entrance tickets are included in that tour package. The Cusco – Lima flight, however, is a domestic flight paid for separately. Package terms remain on the tour page; for a standalone excursion, we agree on price, guide language and start time separately.

## Frequently asked questions

### Which monuments are on the route?

We visit Sacsayhuaman, Coricancha and Tambomachay, with an outside view of neighboring Puka Pukara.

### Can this excursion be combined with a flight to Lima?

On our 15-day tour, it takes place on the day of the Cusco – Lima flight. For a separate trip, the sightseeing schedule must be coordinated with your flight.

### Is an exact duration specified?

The duration, departure time and return time are agreed when planning your specific journey.

## Tours featuring the Cusco archaeological excursion

Here you will find journeys that include our [Sacsayhuaman, Coricancha and Tambomachay excursion](/peru/cusco/sacsayhuaman-coricancha-tambomachay/). It combines three main visits with an exterior view of neighboring Puka Pukara. When selecting a tour, consider both the monuments and the sequence of the entire Peru segment.

## Peru within a 15-day journey through four countries

The [Brazil, Argentina, Chile and Peru tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-peru-15-days/) begins with Rio de Janeiro, Iguazu Falls, Buenos Aires, Santiago and the Chilean coast. You then fly to Cusco and continue into the Sacred Valley of the Incas.

Day twelve is devoted to the valley: Urubamba, Pisac, Ollantaytambo, Chinchero, Moray and Awanakancha. On the following day, we take the Vistadome train to Machu Picchu and return to Cusco after visiting the site.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_braziliya_argentina_chili_peru_ru}}

## Where the Cusco excursion fits into the schedule

After breakfast on day fourteen, you visit [Sacsayhuaman](/peru/place/sacsayhuaman/), [Coricancha](/peru/place/coricancha/) and [Tambomachay](/peru/place/tambomachay/). This continues the exploration of Inca architecture after the valley and Machu Picchu: massive stonework, an urban temple complex and water channels.

After the excursion, you head to the airport and fly to Lima. Peru's capital is scheduled for one night and a city tour before the international departure. The entire journey therefore lasts 15 days and 14 nights, and Cusco is not the final city on the route.

## What to consider when comparing prices

Our package includes hotels with breakfast, transfers, excursions, entrance tickets and the Vistadome train ticket. Domestic flights, including Cusco – Lima, are charged separately. Check the tour page for package inclusions and accommodation rates.

Puka Pukara is viewed from the outside near Tambomachay during this excursion.

## Frequently asked questions

### Are Machu Picchu and the Cusco excursion on the same day?

Not on our 15-day tour. Machu Picchu is visited on day thirteen, while Sacsayhuaman, Coricancha and Tambomachay are on day fourteen.

### Where does the journey end?

After Cusco, the route continues to Lima. The international flight is scheduled to leave Lima on day fifteen, after the city tour and airport transfer.

### Are admission tickets included?

Yes. Entrance tickets for the scheduled sightseeing are included in this tour package. Flights are a separate expense.

## Titicaca Train from Cusco to Puno: across the high Andes

**Titicaca Train** is a rail route between [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) and [Puno on Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/). Travelers spend a full day in transit with views of the Andean plateau, valleys and peaks. The train is valued as an experience in its own right: people choose it for the passing scenery as much as for reaching the next city.

We offer the Titicaca Train **instead of the Cusco – Puno bus journey**. This substitution costs **$295 extra per person**. The train experience includes a dining car, bar, panoramic car, a stop near [La Raya](/peru/place/la-raya-pass/) and a lunch with starter, main course and dessert.

## Views along the route: from Cusco's valleys to the Puno plateau

After departure from Cusco, the landscape changes: green valleys give way to the open spaces of the high-altitude Altiplano. It is striking how different conditions are along a relatively short stretch between two Andean cities.

A recognizable point along the route is [La Raya Pass](/peru/place/la-raya-pass/), more than 4,300 m above sea level. The operator lists a tourist stop near an elevation of 4,335 m. High mountains, sparse vegetation and wide horizons make a memorable scene, but also serve as a reminder of the altitude.

Even a short stop at this elevation feels different from walking at sea level. Some travelers experience discomfort at high altitude. When planning the trip, consider how well you have acclimatized to Cusco and avoid combining strenuous physical activities with a busy transfer day.

## Panoramic car and lunch on board

This is more than an ordinary intercity train. In addition to passenger seats, the operator describes a restaurant car, bar and viewing area. You can enjoy the scenery, move to the restaurant for lunch and return to watching the mountains.

**Our option includes a three-course lunch:** a starter, main course and dessert. This differs from the bus trip, with its own meal and stopping arrangements. The precise menu, drinks, rules for accessing the panoramic car and entertainment should be confirmed for your travel date: not everything advertised by the train operator is automatically included in the commercial package.

The train is expected to reach Puno at about 19:00. The itinerary then includes a transfer and hotel check-in. Actual arrival time depends on railway operations and the carrier's timetable.

## Train or bus between Cusco and Puno?

On the [12-day Peru and Bolivia journey](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-uyuni-12-days/), the standard program uses a bus journey with stops at historic landmarks. It has a separate excursion called [From Cusco to Puno: Andahuaylillas, Raqchi and La Raya](/peru/cusco/cusco-puno-andes-bus/).

| Bus | Titicaca Train |
|---|---|
| Stops along the road | Views from railway cars |
| Visits to sites on the route | Panoramic rail journey |
| Standard transfer option | Alternative with a supplement |

If you prefer ancient settlements, churches and archaeology along the road, the bus itinerary is the better fit. If you would rather watch the Andes from the train for much of the day and eat in the dining car, choose Titicaca Train. **Selecting one option does not automatically preserve every stop from the other.**

## Timetable and onward connections

For our route, the guide is departures **on Wednesdays, Fridays and Sundays** between Cusco and Puno, according to the carrier's schedule. The return direction may have different arrangements. Verify the timetable, boarding station and actual travel date before finalizing flights, accommodation and onward plans.

This train goes to Puno, not Machu Picchu. [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) is served by other rail routes and has separate ticket arrangements. Train names from the same operator's range should not be confused.

After arriving in [Puno](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), you can continue toward Lake Titicaca, but the evening after a full travel day is better left for transfers and rest. Avoid scheduling a lengthy obligatory activity immediately after arrival.

## Who will enjoy Titicaca Train?

The rail journey is especially appealing to those who enjoy landscapes and photography and prefer a relaxed daytime transfer with an organized meal. Boarding comfort, luggage allowances and the ability to move between cars should be agreed in advance.

On a short trip confined to Cusco's surroundings, a full day on the train may be excessive; on an itinerary already continuing toward Lake Titicaca, it is a meaningful alternative to the road.

## Frequently asked questions about Titicaca Train

### How much does replacing the bus with the train cost?

On this specific Ada Tours itinerary, the supplement is **$295 per person**. It is not a universal price for a standalone railway ticket.

### Is lunch included?

Yes. A starter, main course and dessert are specified. Drinks and additional services should be confirmed against the selected arrangements.

### Does the train stop at La Raya?

The published itinerary includes a stop near [La Raya](/peru/place/la-raya-pass/), a high point between Cusco and Puno. The actual stopping pattern is set by the operator.

### Can I continue to Lake Titicaca?

Yes. The train ends this section in Puno, from which separate excursions on [Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/) can be arranged. Those excursions should not be assumed to be included in the rail fare.

## Excursions in Peru: Cusco, Machu Picchu, Titicaca and the coast

In [Peru](/peru/), standalone excursions vary in more than their subject matter: they also take place under very different geographical conditions. A trip from [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) to ancient Inca monuments calls for different planning from a sea excursion near [Paracas](/peru/place/paracas/). Andean altitude, seasons, travel time and visitor restrictions can affect an itinerary more than the total number of attractions listed.

Our catalog includes cultural, historical, nature-focused and active excursions. Start by choosing a base city, your main interest and how much time you can spend traveling. Then compare actual services: familiar landmark names do not by themselves prove that admissions or transfers are included.

## Cusco and Machu Picchu: two distinct experiences

[Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) is rewarding as a historic city. The [Cusco and Sacsayhuaman excursion](/peru/cusco/cusco-sacsayhuaman-archaeological-tour/) combines urban architecture with nearby archaeological complexes, including Qenqo, Puka Pukara and Tambomachay. Visitor timing, altitude and walking pace all matter on this program.

[Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) is a separate journey. Our [full-day excursion from Cusco](/peru/cusco/machu-picchu-day-tour-from-cusco/) includes a train journey and a bus climb to the ancient city. The logistics are much more extensive than those of a walk through Cusco's central neighborhoods.

Machu Picchu visits follow approved circuits and entry time slots; the ticket type determines which areas can be accessed. When booking, confirm the specific circuit, visiting slot and ticket arrangements. Rules change: even a ticket to "Machu Picchu" does not necessarily grant access to every zone.

## The Sacred Valley: archaeology and varied formats

The [Sacred Valley of the Incas](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/) adds settlements and agricultural terraces to a Cusco trip. For example, a [group excursion through Chinchero, Moray and Ollantaytambo](/peru/cusco/sacred-valley-chinchero-moray-ollantaytambo-group-tour/) offers a broader valley experience than a single city temple visit.

For those seeking physical activities, the catalog features separate offerings: [via ferrata in the Sacred Valley](/peru/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/peru-sacred-valley-via-ferrata/) and [ziplining](/peru/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/peru-sacred-valley-zipline/). These differ from standard monument excursions in fitness requirements, equipment and weather restrictions. Adventure activities should not be assumed to be included in every Sacred Valley tour.

## Arequipa and Colca Canyon: watching condors

From [Arequipa](/peru/place/arequipa/), excursions head to Colca Canyon, one of the Andes' well-known natural areas. The [canyon and condor viewpoint excursion](/peru/arequipa/colca-canyon-condor-tour-from-arequipa/) is a day trip with an early departure. Its route crosses highland areas and visits the Cruz del Condor viewpoint.

Condors live freely in the wild, so sightings near the viewpoint cannot be guaranteed, even under favorable conditions. Start time, elevation changes, sun and early-morning cold are particularly important. If the itinerary includes long mountain transfers, avoid linking it too closely to an evening flight.

## Puno and Lake Titicaca

Around [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), cultural encounters focus on local communities and travel by water. The [one-day Uros and Taquile Islands excursion](/peru/puno-and-lake-titicaca/lake-titicaca-uros-islands-day-tour/) is described as a boat trip returning to Puno.

This differs markedly from Cusco's archaeological sites. Lake conditions, transfers between islands and time spent learning about local traditions define much of the day. Check which stops are included, the format of community visits and any additional expenses.

## Lima and the Pacific: museum, city or marine islands

[Lima](/peru/place/lima/) is a starting point for urban culture. A [Lima sightseeing tour](/peru/lima/lima-city-tour-4-hours/) lasts four hours. A separate [Larco Museum excursion](/peru/lima/larco-museum-lima-tour/) focuses on archaeological collections. These are two different formats, and museum entry is not necessarily included in every city tour.

Another Pacific-coast attraction is the [Ballestas Islands excursion](/peru/paracas/ballestas-islands-tour/) from Paracas, focused on marine wildlife observed from a boat. Weather and sea conditions can affect departures.

A separate itinerary can include a [flight over the Nazca Lines](/peru/nazca-lines-and-ballestas-islands/nazca-lines-flight/). Check the departure airport, flight format and weather conditions; it is not an obligatory part of a Paracas journey.

## A quick guide by interest

| Region | Main appeal |
|---|---|
| Cusco | Inca heritage |
| Sacred Valley | Terraces, monuments and adventure |
| Colca | Mountain views and condors |
| Titicaca | Lake and community culture |
| Lima / Paracas | City and marine nature |

In Peru, **altitude differences between regions** are particularly important. Conditions on the coast and during Andean excursions vary, so plan time for acclimatization, transfers and physical exertion. For multiple regions, start by exploring [Peru tours](/peru/tour/) and then identify which standalone excursions are already included.

## What to check before booking an excursion

Confirm the exact departure and return locations, guiding language, duration, admissions and transport. Machu Picchu requires an identified entry circuit; active mountain excursions have participant requirements; marine trips depend on weather and cancellation rules.

Do not apply one excursion's terms to another: a train excursion to Machu Picchu is different from sightseeing only in Cusco, and a Titicaca tour does not necessarily offer the same services as a coastal boat trip.

## Frequently asked questions about excursions in Peru

### Can Machu Picchu be visited in one day from Cusco?

Yes. Ada Tours offers a [one-day itinerary with train and bus transport](/peru/cusco/machu-picchu-day-tour-from-cusco/). It is a busy day, and tickets and service schedules should be checked in advance.

### Do I need time to adapt to altitude before an excursion?

For highland areas around Cusco, Colca and Titicaca, acclimatization time matters. Plan a pace suited to how you feel, and discuss the itinerary with a doctor if there are medical considerations.

### Where is better for watching animals: Colca or Paracas?

[Colca](/peru/arequipa/colca-canyon-condor-tour-from-arequipa/) is known for Andean condors, while the [Ballestas Islands](/peru/paracas/ballestas-islands-tour/) feature marine wildlife. They are different ecosystems and excursions.

### Are all admission tickets included?

There is no single rule for the catalog. Confirm admission, meals, transport and guiding services in the terms of each specific offering.
